# Baigana poda

By Ahimanikya Satapathy

Roasted garlic or raw additions; flame or broiler.

Pragyan suggests putting garlic into slots in the eggplant before roasting. After peeling and mashing, roasted garlic, onion, ginger, cream and green chilli are added. The account also offers an oven alternative: this is one cook’s preparation, not a regional formula.[^1]

Away in the Kitchen recalls a mother roasting eggplant and tomato over a flame. The writer adapts that preparation to a broiler, describing it as familiar but not smoky. The peeled vegetables are mashed with uncooked onion, garlic and chilli, then finished with mustard oil.[^2]

The photograph shows combined eggplant and tomato, baigana-bilati poda. It is not a photograph of either recipe described here.

[^1]: Pragyan, “Some Odiya Roasted Dishes,” Sorisha, 12 October 2008.
[^2]: Away in the Kitchen, “Baingan Chokha | Baigana Poda,” 26 August 2020; updated 25 January 2021.
